newsitem.title: CHINA: Huili says changing market hit profits.
newsitem.headline: Huili says changing market hit profits.

text.p: Shanghai Huili Building Materials Co said on Friday that changing market conditions which forced the firm to adjust its product mix were responsible for its profit dive in 1996.
In its annual results issued on Thursday, the company said its net profit fell 67.7 percent to 15.727 million yuan in 1996 from 48.695 million yuan for 1995, based on domestic accounting standards.
Based on international accounting standards, the 1996 net was only 6.512 million yuan against 48.028 million in 1995.

With improvements in living standards, demand for the firm's traditional products such as multi-coloured coatings decreased sharply. It was forced to produce more emulsion paints, which are less profitable, the firm said in its annual report.
The company had invested heavily in new projects including floorboards and wooden doors, but they have not yet started to yield returns, the report said.
The company's board of directors have proposed no cash dividend or bonus share issue, pending approval at a shareholders meeting scheduled for June 10.
The annual report said the company would make profitability its prime task in 1997, and strive to boost net profits by more than 50 percent against 1996. It gave no details.
